articles.title: Bengaluru road rage: Man follows woman to her friend’s apartment, attacks her with bucket
articles.summary: Bengaluru road rage: Scooter rider allegedly followed a woman to an apartment and attacked her with an object and paint bucket; police probe CCTV, case filed.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A narrow escape from a road accident turned into a terrifying ordeal for a 30-year-old woman in Banashankari when a scooter-borne man, whom she had confronted for driving on the wrong side, allegedly chased her to friend’s apartment and launched a vicious attack. He allegedly hit her with a hard object and an empty paint bucket, targeting her head, shoulder, arms and face, while hurling obscene and derogatory abuses.According to the complaint filed by Meena (name changed), a research scholar and resident of Banashankari 3rd Stage, the incident occurred at 10am on Oct 30. She had gone for a workout at a gym and was riding her scooter towards her friend’s apartment when the incident unfolded.On the way, a man riding a scooter with a woman as pillion allegedly approached at high speed from the wrong direction and nearly rammed into her vehicle. Meena narrowly avoided the collision and questioned him over his reckless driving. After the argument, Meena continued towards her friend’s apartment. However, the man allegedly followed her. Even after she reached the apartment and parked her scooter outside, he approached her and assaulted her. She told him not to come near her and rushed inside the apartment. Carrying a bag containing an object, he followed her inside. He attacked her several times on the head, shoulder, arm and forearm, leaving her injured.Even as the man’s wife reportedly tried to restrain him, he picked up an empty paint bucket and struck Meena on the face and neck. The commotion eventually drew the attention of residents and Meena’s friend, who rushed to the spot around 10.15am and questioned the man about his actions. articles.title: Bengaluru-Goa Vande Bharat to impact 13 trains on coastal route
articles.summary: Bengaluru–Goa Vande Bharat (26655/26656) may be introduced from Yeshwantpur, but could reschedule 13 coastal trains, affecting regular passengers’ timings.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A faster, more comfortable ride on Vande Bharat Express from Bengaluru to Goa is on the cards, but its introduction may lead to rescheduling of 13 existing trains and disrupting passenger-friendly arrival and departure timings.Last Saturday, the railway ministry notified the introduction of Vande Bharat service between Yeshwantpur and Madgaon, assigning numbers 26655 and 26656. The Vande Bharat will operate six days a week from Yeshwantpur, departing at 7.35am, except on Wednesdays.A railway official said to facilitate 1,100 passengers on Vande Bharat, around 15,000 regular travellers will be affected. A senior South Western Railway official said the new service would be accorded priority through the ghat section.The train will traverse the recently electrified ghat section between Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road, a 55km stretch where all trains are restricted to a maximum speed of 30kmph because of the challenging terrain and safety concerns.Among the biggest casualties would be train No. 16516 Karwar-Yeshwantpur Express. The train, which currently reaches Bengaluru at 8.50pm, will arrive at 10.15pm under the revised schedule.An even bigger blow awaits passengers travelling on train No. 16576 Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur Gomteshwara Express. A popular option for passengers travelling from Mangaluru to Bengaluru, the train currently reaches Yeshwantpur at 4.30pm. Under the revised schedule, it will leave Mangaluru at 11.40am and reach Bengaluru at 10.15pm.The change also takes away much of the convenience of its existing schedule for passengers planning to reach Bengaluru by late afternoon. The train, which has a vistadome coach offering panoramic views of the Western Ghats, will continue to provide the scenic experience, but at a considerably different time of day.In another notable change, train No. 22679 Yeshwantpur-Hassan Superfast Express will see its average speed fall below 55kmph in both directions. articles.title: Enem: ônibus terão operação especial em Campo Grande nos dias de prova | G1
articles.standfirst: A linha 222 terá horários de sábado nos dias 8 e 15 de novembro. Terminais também contarão com veículos extras para atender aos candidatos que farão o exame.
articles.summary: A linha 222 terá horários de sábado nos dias 8 e 15 de novembro. Terminais também contarão com veículos extras para atender aos candidatos que farão o exame.
articles.body:
Enem terá ônibus extras em Campo Grande nos dias de prova — Foto: PMCG

A Agência Municipal de Transporte e Trânsito (Agetran) preparou uma operação especial no transporte coletivo de Campo Grande para os domingos de aplicação do Enem 2026, nos dias 8 e 15 de novembro. A medida prevê mudanças nos horários de uma das linhas e ônibus extras nos terminais para facilitar o deslocamento dos candidatos até os locais de prova.

Nas duas datas, a linha 222 (T. General Osório / Ucdb) vai funcionar com a programação de sábado, das 7h25 às 19h35. As demais linhas seguirão os horários habituais de domingos e feriados.

Além dos ônibus que já circulam normalmente, haverá veículos extras com motoristas e demais integrantes da equipe nos terminais, das 8h às 18h.

No Terminal General Osório, serão dois ônibus extras, além dos dois que já ficam disponíveis, totalizando quatro veículos de reserva. Nos outros terminais, haverá um veículo extra, somando três ônibus disponíveis em cada local.

O Consórcio Guaicurus, responsável pelo transporte coletivo da capital, deverá acompanhar a movimentação e ajustar os intervalos entre os ônibus nos horários de maior concentração de candidatos, caso seja necessário ou por determinação da fiscalização da Agetran.

A agência também vai monitorar o funcionamento do transporte em tempo real para identificar possíveis aumentos na demanda e orientar mudanças durante os dias de prova.

articles.title: Sessão para julgar impeachment de Santiago Peña começa no Paraguai | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente havia pedido mais 72 horas para apresentar defesa. Sessão do Senado aberta nesta sexta-feira rejeitou solicitação e retomará julgamento do impeachment (5). Para afastá-lo, são necessários ao menos 30 votos entre os 45 senadores que compõem comissão especial.
articles.summary: Presidente havia pedido mais 72 horas para apresentar defesa. Sessão do Senado aberta nesta sexta-feira rejeitou solicitação e retomará julgamento do impeachment (5). Para afastá-lo, são necessários ao menos 30 votos entre os 45 senadores que compõem comissão especial.
articles.body:
O Senado do Paraguai rejeitou nesta sexta-feira (6) o pedido do presidente do país, Santiago Peña , para que adiassem o julgamento do processo de impeachment contra o presidente.

Peña deveria apresentar sua defesa em uma sessão no Senado iniciada nesta sexta, mas pediu mais tempo para preparar argumentos. Em votação na sessão, os senadores rejeitaram o pedido e retomarão o processo de impeachment ainda nesta sexta.

➡️ Peña está no centro da crise bancária que tomou o Paraguai. Ele é acusado de ter sido conivente com a quebra do banco digital ueno, que encerrou atividades e deixou mais de um terço da população paraguaia sem acesso às suas contas bancárias. Pressionado pela oposição e isolado por seus próprios aliados, o presidente apresentou renúncia na quinta-feira (5), ainda não aceita pelo Congresso.

O processo de impeachment, aberto na Câmara dos Deputados também na quinta, corre em paralelo à carta de renúncia apresentada por Peña — a renúncia não é automática, e cabe ao Congresso aceitá-la ou rejeitá-la.

Já a sessão iniciada nesta sexta é dedicada à apresentação da defesa do presidente. Nesta manhã, no entanto, o presidente paraguaio pediu mais tempo para apresentar sua defesa . Peña solicitou 72 horas adicionais para ler a acusação e preparar seu argumento.

Em votação, senadores rejeitaram em maioria ampla adiar o julgamento. O pleno registrou 39 votos contra o adiamento, três a favor e duas abstenções .

Com o resultado, os senadores retomarão a sessão ainda nesta sexta, mas ainda não havia previsão, até a última atualização desta reportagem, da votação do impeachment, que afastaria Santiago Peña sem os privilégios concedidos a presidentes que terminam sem mandato normalmente.

O presidente do Congresso paraguaio, Basilio Núñez, havia afirmado na quinta-feira a jornalistas que não seria possível concluir o julgamento em apenas um dia . Segundo Núñez, o processo de impechament ocorrerá em cinco fases. A sessão desta sexta foi a segunda fase, e ainda não havia previsão para as outras três sessões.

Depois da manifestação de Peña nesta sexta, os senadores deverão analisar as provas apresentadas pela acusação e pela defesa. Na sequência, as partes terão a oportunidade de apresentar seus argumentos finais. Só então os 45 integrantes do Senado votarão o impeachment.

Para afastar Peña definitivamente, serão necessários pelo menos 30 votos favoráveis , o equivalente a dois terços dos senadores. Se condenado, ele perderá o mandato e também deixará de ter direito à condição de senador vitalício.

➡️ No Paraguai, ex-presidentes que concluíram seus mandatos ou renunciaram ao cargo ganham o título de senador vitalício, o que garante imunidade parlamentar pelo resto da vida. Neste caso, no entanto, ex-líderes que sejam "condenados em julgamentos políticos" terão esse direito revogado.

Caso o impeachment seja aprovado, o vice-presidente Pedro Alliana assumirá a Presidência e deverá concluir o mandato, que termina em agosto de 2028. Se Peña for absolvido, preservará o cargo de senador.

presidente Santiago Peña, a quem culpam pela crise desencadeada pelo colapso do banco digital Ueno, que deixou milhões de clientes sem acesso às suas contas, em Assunção, Paraguai, 5 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Cesar Olmedo

O processo de impeachment ocorre após a quebra do banco ueno , pertencente ao Grupo Vázquez. A instituição fechou as portas na última terça-feira (3), depois que o Banco Central paraguaio iniciou sua liquidação por insuficiência de recursos para cobrir as obrigações financeiras.

O banco tinha cerca de 3 milhões de clientes e concentrava aproximadamente US$ 850 milhões em depósitos públicos, incluindo recursos do Instituto de Previdência Social. Peña foi acionista do grupo proprietário da instituição até março de 2025.

Após o escândalo, parlamentares da oposição passaram a acusar o presidente por um suposto conflito de interesses, manipulação de regras e irregularidades envolvendo recursos previdenciários. A acusação também aponta que o Banco Central teria encoberto problemas financeiros da instituição.

Santiago Peña, presidente do Paraguai desde 2023 que apresentou renao cargo em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Cesar Olmedo/File Photo

Momentos depois, o presidente apresentou uma carta de renúncia em um vídeo, em que se desculpou com a população que perdeu o acesso ao próprio dinheiro e disse que decidiu renunciar "pensando na estabilidade do nosso país, na paz social e na necessidade de preservar nossas instituições democráticas".

"Estou convencido de que nenhum cargo pode estar acima do bem-estar do Paraguai. Também quero pedir desculpas ao povo. Se em algum momento falhei, nunca foi minha intenção decepcionar a confiança que depositaram em mim", disse.

Na sessão conjunta do Congresso que se seguiu, porém, foi colocado em votação o pedido de renúncia do presidente .

A oposição defendia que o Congresso rejeitasse a renúncia e desse continuidade ao impeachment. Os parlamentares argumentavam que a saída voluntária permitiria a Peña assumir uma vaga de senador vitalício, com direito a foro privilegiado.

O senador de oposição Líder Amarilla alegou que aceitar a renúncia poderia impedir que o presidente respondesse a eventuais acusações na Justiça.

"Se aceitarmos esta renúncia, o que estamos fazendo é permitir que Santiago Peña obtenha foro parlamentar e que todo o dinheiro que foi roubado fique impune, porque a Promotoria não poderá apresentar acusações contra ele", disse Amarilla, em entrevista ao ABC Color.

Já os governistas sustentavam que aceitar a saída do presidente seria a maneira mais rápida de encerrar a crise política e permitir a transferência de poder ao vice-presidente, Pedro Alliana.

O grupo também afirmava que o Senado poderia analisar um eventual pedido de retirada do foro de Peña, caso a Promotoria solicitasse a medida.

articles.title: Novas ameaças de bomba afetam voos na Europa | G1
articles.standfirst: Mais de 10 voos emitiram alerta de bomba nesta sexta (6), e dezenas de outros casos foram registrados nesta semana. Até o momento, nenhum explosivo havia sido encontrado. Emissoras irlandesa, britânica e búlgara também receberam alerta de segurança.
articles.summary: Mais de 10 voos emitiram alerta de bomba nesta sexta (6), e dezenas de outros casos foram registrados nesta semana. Até o momento, nenhum explosivo havia sido encontrado. Emissoras irlandesa, britânica e búlgara também receberam alerta de segurança.
articles.body:
Novas ameaças de bomba afetaram mais de 10 voos comerciais na Europa nesta sexta-feira (6) e voltaram a causar pousos de emergência, inspeções de esquadrões antibomba e caos na aviação comercial europeia.

Até o momento, nenhum explosivo foi encontrado e, segundo a agência de notícias Reuters, todas as aeronaves afetadas aterrissaram em segurança.

Ao menos nove voos chegando ou saindo do aeroporto de Praga , na República Tcheca , foram alvo de ameaças de bomba nesta sexta-feira , afirmou um porta-voz do aeroporto à agência de notícias AFP.

Quatro voos que sobrevoavam o território da França nesta sexta emitiram ameaça de bomba , afirmou o gabinete do premiê francês Sebastién Lecornu. Todos os voos pousaram como previsto e foram submetidos a inspeções por esquadrões antibomba.

Na Itália , dois voos, um saindo e outro chegando do aeroporto de Roma emitiram alerta de bomba , segundo a agência de notícias italiana Ansa. Segundo a agência, foram:

Dois voos vindos de Londres e Bruxelas que aterrissaram no aeroporto de Sofia, na Bulgária , nesta sexta também tiveram ameaça de bomba, afirmou o ministro dos Transportes búlgaro.

A Hungria afirmou que mobilizou caças para escoltar três voos que tiveram alerta de bomba : um deles com destino a Sofia, outro a Bucareste, na Romênia, e o último rumo ao Chipre, segundo o ministro da Defesa, Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi.

Este é o terceiro dia nesta semana em que ameaças de bomba surgem em voos internos na Europa, no que autoridades europeias chamaram de "armação maliciosa", "agressão híbrida" e "campanha coordenada". Os alertas desta sexta-feira se juntam a outros cerca de 30 incidentes registrados até quinta-feira. Leia mais abaixo.

Aeronaves na pista do aeroporto internacional de Vaclav Havel, em Praga, capital da República Tcheca, que registrou ameaças de bomba em 6 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/David W Cerny

"As ameaças dizem respeito a voos com chegada da Dinamarca, Espanha e Reino Unido . Quanto aos voos de partida, são voos com destino à Holanda, Chipre, Romênia, Itália e Reino Unido", disse a porta-voz Denisa Hejtmankova à AFP. Ainda segundo ela, nenhum dispositivo havia sido encontrado nos voos inspecionados até o momento.

Segundo a Ansa, um voo Ryanair vindo de Roma, na Itália, e com destino a Lisboa, em Portugal aterrissou como previsto. A polícia portuguesa afirmou que nenhuma bomba foi encontrada a bordo. Já um outro voo, da Wizzair, ia de Praga com destino a Roma quando precisou ser desviado para Veneza.

A polícia da Dinamarca afirmou nesta sexta que estava investigando novas ameaças no aeroporto de Copenhague.

'Agressão híbrida' e 'boato malicioso': a onda de ameaças de bomba em voos comerciais na Europa

Avião Airbus A320 da companhia aérea Aer Lingus após fazer pouso de emergência na base aérea de Évreux, no norte da França, em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Gonzalo Fuentes

Essa onda de ameaças de bomba, junto com o fato de que nenhum explosivo havia sido encontrado, levantou a suspeita de que se trate de um ataque híbrido coordenado da Rússia , que nos últimos meses tem utilizado meios não convencionais para impactar a população europeia. Até o momento, no entanto, as ameaças não haviam sido ligadas explicitamente à Rússia.

Na quinta, a secretária dos Transportes do Reino Unido chamou de "armação maliciosa e mal-intencional" essa onda recente de ameaças de bomba em voos. Já o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Espanha afirmou que o continente parecia estar enfrentando uma "agressão híbrida e uma espécie de guerra psicológica".

Especialistas europeus em segurança também foram na mesma linha e disseram que as ameaças apresentavam características de um "ataque híbrido" coordenado.

O governo russo ainda não havia se posicionado sobre o caso até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Na quinta-feira, mais de 20 voos foram afetados por alerta de bombas. As aeronaves estavam em trechos entre Paris, Praga, Roma, Bruxelas, Milão e aeroportos no leste europeu, e eram de diversas companhias aéreas: Aer Lingus, Wizz Air, LOT, Finnair, EasyJet, Iberia, KLM.

Um deles foi até obrigado a aterrissar em uma base aérea francesa , algo que não é tão comum na aviação civil.

Já na terça-feira, sete voos tiveram ameaças de bomba, além de um cruzeiro com destino a Israel, que foi inspecionado em um porto grego. Na segunda-feira, um voo da Wizzair registrou ameaça de bomba.

Funcionários da emissora pública irlandesa RTE do lado de fora do escritório após ameaça de bomba causar evacuação em 6 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Natalia Campos

Além dos voos, empresas de mídia na Irlanda, do Reino Unido, e da Bulgária também receberam nesta sexta-feira alertas de bomba e evacuaram seus funcionários para inspeções antibomba.

Na Irlanda, a emissora pública RTE foi afetada. O veículo afirmou que a ameaça ocorreu via e-mail e pode ter relação com os incidentes que têm afetado os voos.

O governo da Irlanda afirmou que as ameaças contra os voos pela Europa e contra as emissoras irlandesas provavelmente fazem parte de uma "campanha coordenada de desestabilização". "As ameaças feitas nesta manhã contra organizações de mídia [irlandesas] são muito sérias. (...) Ameaças falsas como essas causam medo e inquietação e interrompem a rotina das pessoas", disse.

A emissora britânica Sky News informou que também recebeu uma "ameaça à sua segurança", o que causou uma inspeção nas instalações.

Na Bulgária, a emissora privada Nova TV também teve que evacuar seus funcionários após receber e-mails com alerta de bomba.

Segundo a TV búlgara, o e-mail recebido tinha título "mensagem ao Oeste" e era assinado por uma pessoa chamada "Mikhail Andropov", que também reivindicava responsabilidade pelos alertas nos voos pela Europa.

articles.title: Pequim denuncia 'sabotagem' dos EUA às relações Cuba-China | G1
articles.standfirst: Reação vem após novas sanções econômicas norte-americanas contra Cuba terem incluído pela primeira vez duas empresas chinesas. Governo Trump realiza campanha de pressão contra o governo da ilha caribenha.
articles.summary: Reação vem após novas sanções econômicas norte-americanas contra Cuba terem incluído pela primeira vez duas empresas chinesas. Governo Trump realiza campanha de pressão contra o governo da ilha caribenha.
articles.body:
Xi Jinping e Donald Trump durante encontro na Casa Branca — Foto: Reuters/Evan Vucci

O governo da China denunciou nesta sexta-feira (6) como "sabotagem" as novas sanções dos Estados Unidos contra Cuba , que incluem pela primeira vez duas empresas do país asiático.

A nova rodada de sanções, anunciada na quinta-feira, concentra-se no setor de petróleo e tecnologia da ilha, contra a qual Washington lançou uma estratégia de pressão econômica.

Entre as empresas afetadas estão as companhias eletrônicas chinesas CEIEC e Beijing H&C Technologies, que Washington acusa de vender material de defesa e sistemas de segurança para Cuba .

"A China se opõe de modo veemente à interferência e à sabotagem dos Estados Unidos na cooperação entre China e Cuba ", declarou em entrevista coletiva o porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores, Guo Jiakun.

Jiakun também advertiu que a China adotara "todas as medidas necessárias" para salvaguardar os interesses de suas empresas na ilha caribenha.

Desde janeiro, o governo dos Estados Unidos impôs duras sanções e um bloqueio de petróleo contra Cuba , o que paralisou a economia do país e provocou apagões generalizados e escassez de produtos.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, chegou a insinuar a possibilidade de lançar uma intervenção militar para derrubar o Partido Comunista que governa a ilha.

Papai Noel — Foto: Tatiana Ferro/Divulgação

O Natal ainda está a algumas semanas de distância, mas o Papai Noel já tem data marcada para chegar aos shoppings da região de Campinas (SP).

A programação começa nesta sexta-feira (6) e reúne atrações gratuitas para toda a família, com espetáculos, desfiles, música e inauguração de decorações temáticas.

Ao todo, oito shoppings de Campinas, Hortolândia , Indaiatuba e Sumaré já anunciaram as datas de chegada do Bom Velhinho. O primeiro evento será no Shopping Parque Dom Pedro, em Campinas, nesta sexta-feira, às 19h30.

A programação pode ser atualizada conforme novos eventos forem anunciados.

articles.summary: Lojas de rua poderão abrir das 8h às 14h, enquanto estabelecimentos em shoppings estão autorizados a funcionar das 13h às 21h.
articles.body:
Rua Grande é a principal rua de comércio popular em São Luís, Maranhão — Foto: A. Baeta/Prefeitura de São Luís

O comércio de São Luís está autorizado a funcionar no próximo dia 15 de novembro, feriado nacional da Proclamação da República. A informação foi divulgada pela Federação do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo do Estado do Maranhão (Fecomércio-MA).

De acordo com a entidade, a autorização segue um acordo firmado com o Sindicato dos Empregados no Comércio de São Luís (Sindcomerciários), que estabelece horários específicos para o funcionamento dos estabelecimentos comerciais na capital maranhense.

Lojas de rua, avenidas, galerias e centros comerciais: das 8h às 14h;

Lojas em shopping centers: das 13h às 21h.

Segundo a Fecomércio-MA, os funcionários convocados para trabalhar no feriado terão direito ao pagamento das horas trabalhadas com acréscimo de 100% sobre o valor da hora normal, além de uma gratificação de R$ 53.

As empresas que decidirem abrir também deverão comunicar previamente ao Sindcomerciários a relação dos empregados escalados para trabalhar na data.

Além disso, será necessário recolher uma taxa de R$ 13 por funcionário em atividade, conforme as condições estabelecidas no acordo entre as entidades.

A abertura dos estabelecimentos é facultativa, desde que sejam respeitadas as regras previstas no acordo trabalhista.

articles.title: Homem tenta roubar foragido da Justiça e os dois acabam presos | G1
articles.standfirst: Suspeito foi detido por tentativa de roubo e um jovem, apontado como vítima, era procurado pela Justiça por homicídio.
articles.summary: Caso aconteceu no bairro Aterrado, em Volta Redonda.
articles.body:
Homem tenta roubar foragido da Justiça e ambos acabam presos em Volta Redonda — Foto: Divulgação/Guarda Municipal de Volta Redonda (GMVR)

Dois homens foram presos após uma tentativa de roubo na manhã de quinta-feira (5), no bairro Aterrado, em Volta Redonda (RJ). O suspeito, de 25 anos, foi detido por tentativa de roubo. Já o jovem apontado como vítima, de 22 anos, era procurado pela Justiça por homicídio.

Segundo a Guarda Municipal, agentes foram alertados por moradores sobre uma briga na Avenida Lucas Evangelista, por volta das 10h50. No local, encontraram o jovem de 22 anos imobilizando o outro homem.

Ainda de acordo com a Guarda, testemunhas relataram que o suspeito tentou roubar o celular e a vítima reagiu, entrando em luta corporal. Os dois tiveram escoriações e receberam atendimento médico antes de serem levados à delegacia de Volta Redonda.

Na unidade policial, o suspeito de 25 anos foi autuado por tentativa de roubo. Durante a identificação do jovem de 22 anos, os policiais descobriram que ele havia tentado se passar por outra pessoa. Após consulta aos sistemas judiciais, foi constatado um mandado de prisão em aberto por homicídio.

Os dois permaneceram presos e à disposição da Justiça.

articles.title: Homem é condenado a 28 anos por matar ex-companheira em Parnaíba | G1
articles.standfirst: Crime ocorreu em 2023, após o ocorrido, Marcos Gustavo fugiu e foi localizado no Ceará.
articles.summary: O feminicídio em Parnaíba ocorreu em 2023, quando Aline Vasconcelos foi morta ao sair do trabalho; Marcos Gustavo foi preso no Ceará e condenado nesta quarta-feira.
articles.body:
Marcos Gustavo Laviola Nobre foi condenado a 28 anos de prisão pelo assassinato da ex-companheira, Aline Vasconcelos Silva, morta a tiros em abril de 2023 em um posto de combustíveis de Parnaíba . A sentença foi definida na quarta-feira (4).

Segundo o Ministério Público do Estado do Piauí (MPPI), a investigação apontou que Marcos não aceitava o fim do relacionamento.

De acordo com o órgão, a vítima havia saído do trabalho para almoçar quando foi abordada pelo ex-companheiro.

Um vídeo de uma câmera de segurança do estabelecimento registrou o crime. As imagens mostram Aline tentando subir na garupa de uma motocicleta conduzida por outra pessoa. (assista o vídeo no início da reportagem).

Em seguida, Marcos chega armado e atira contra a vítima, que cai no chão após os disparos.

Após o crime, Marcos fugiu do local. Segundo o MPPI, Marcos foi localizado e preso em Granja , no Ceará.

Ele foi condenado por homicídio qualificado por motivo torpe, pelo uso de recurso que impossibilitou a defesa da vítima e por feminicídio.

articles.title: UE exige que TikTok mude feeds personalizados por possíveis efeitos nocivos | G1
articles.standfirst: A plataforma já está sob suspeita de ter cometido outras infrações a esse mesmo regulamento, incluindo o descumprimento de suas obrigações de proteção a menores.
articles.summary: A plataforma já está sob suspeita de ter cometido outras infrações a esse mesmo regulamento, incluindo o descumprimento de suas obrigações de proteção a menores.
articles.body:
Ícone do aplicativo de compartilhamento de vídeos TikTok. — Foto: AP/Matt Slocum/Arquivo

A União Europeia exigiu, nesta sexta-feira (6), que o TikTok faça mudanças profundas em seus fluxos de vídeos personalizados, que, segundo o bloco, podem prejudicar o bem-estar e a saúde mental dos usuários ao expô-los repetidamente a conteúdos com efeitos negativos.

A subsidiária do grupo chinês ByteDance pode receber uma multa porque, segundo a Comissão Europeia, a empresa pode ter violado regras fundamentais da Lei de Serviços Digitais (DSA).

A legislação, que estabelece regras para conteúdos, é uma das principais ferramentas jurídicas adotadas pela UE nos últimos anos para regular as grandes empresas de tecnologia.

No centro da questão está o funcionamento do sistema do TikTok que recomenda conteúdos aos usuários.

Os fluxos de vídeos personalizados são projetados para exibir repetidamente conteúdos que tenham despertado o interesse do usuário. Isso inclui temas que, quando consumidos de forma recorrente, podem afetar o bem-estar físico e moral, como tristeza, solidão e questões relacionadas à autoestima.

Segundo a Comissão Europeia, o consumo contínuo e repetido desse tipo de conteúdo pode ter efeitos negativos sobre a saúde mental, especialmente entre adultos vulneráveis e menores de idade.

➡️ O fenômeno é conhecido em inglês como "rabbit holes" , expressão usada para descrever situações em que o usuário é levado a consumir cada vez mais conteúdos sobre um mesmo tema.

A rede social já fez mudanças em seus fluxos personalizados, mas a Comissão Europeia considera que as medidas não são suficientes. Por isso, exige que o TikTok faça alterações profundas que atingem o próprio modelo de negócio da plataforma, baseado em manter a atenção dos usuários pelo maior tempo possível.

A exigência está relacionada à forma como o sistema seleciona os conteúdos exibidos aos usuários.

Segundo a Comissão Europeia, mesmo quando um usuário indica que não tem mais interesse em determinado tipo de conteúdo, o sistema do TikTok pode ignorar essa escolha para aumentar o tempo que ele passa na plataforma.

"A Comissão formulou uma série de afirmações fundamentalmente inexatas", reagiu um porta-voz do grupo à AFP. "Temos um histórico comprovado na proteção da nossa comunidade", acrescentou a plataforma.

O TikTok também é investigado por suspeitas de outras violações do mesmo regulamento, entre elas o possível descumprimento das obrigações de proteção de menores, o que pode aumentar os riscos de assédio no ambiente digital e de exposição a possíveis predadores.

A UE ampliou as medidas para regular as redes sociais com base no DSA e pretende proibir o acesso a essas plataformas por menores de 13 anos devido aos riscos para o bem-estar e o desenvolvimento desse público.

articles.title: Justiça autoriza três bets a voltar a funcionar em SP, e desembargadora chama proibição do governo federal de 'verdadeiro confisco' | G1
articles.standfirst: Fim das bets foi anunciado pela presidente Lula (PT) em medida provisória de 120 dias publicada em 25 de setembro, 9 dias antes do 1° turno da eleição presidencial. Decisão beneficia Casa de Apostas, Betsul e Jogo Online e prevê multa diária de R$ 200 mil ao governo federal em caso de descumprimento.
articles.summary: Fim das bets foi anunciado pela presidente Lula (PT) em medida provisória de 120 dias publicada em 25 de setembro, 9 dias antes do 1° turno da eleição presidencial. Decisão beneficia Casa de Apostas, Betsul e Jogo Online e prevê multa diária de R$ 200 mil ao governo federal em caso de descumprimento.
articles.body:
O Tribunal Regional Federal da 3ª Região (TRF-3), em São Paulo , autorizou três casas de apostas a voltar a funcionar no Brasil a partir desta quinta-feira (5). A decisão prevê multa de R$ 200 mil por dia ao governo federal caso a determinação não seja cumprida.

Na decisão, a desembargadora Adriana Pileggi afirmou que proibir o funcionamento de empresas que receberam autorização do próprio governo, sem indenizá-las pelos prejuízos, representa um “verdadeiro confisco”.

A medida beneficia três plataformas da empresa CDA Gaming: Casa de Apostas, Betsul e Jogo Online. A companhia entrou na Justiça para contestar a medida provisória editada pelo presidente Lula (PT) que proibiu as bets no país , pouco antes do primeiro turno das eleições presidenciais.

Na manhã desta sexta-feira (6), o site da Casa de Apostas, uma das três plataformas beneficiadas pela decisão judicial, já estava funcionando novamente . A empresa havia sido impedida de operar no país após a proibição das bets pelo governo federal.

A Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU) afirmou que irá recorrer da decisão do Tribunal Regional Federal da 3ª Região (TRF3) que liberou o funcionamento de casas de apostas on-line da empresa CDA Gaming.

A empresa teve o pedido negado duas vezes por juízes federais, mas recorreu ao TRF-3 e conseguiu uma liminar, que é uma decisão provisória. A autorização vale apenas para as três bets da empresa, enquanto as demais continuam proibidas. Já o Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) analisa ações que questionam a proibição das apostas em todo o país. ( Leia mais abaixo) .

Para a desembargadora, o governo deu um prazo muito curto para que as empresas encerrassem suas atividades, sem considerar os investimentos feitos para obter autorização e operar legalmente no Brasil.

Na decisão, ela argumentou que as empresas receberam permissão do governo para funcionar e gastaram dinheiro com equipamentos, tecnologia e estrutura. Por isso, segundo ela, não poderiam ser obrigadas a encerrar as operações de forma tão repentina.

A magistrada também questionou a justificativa do governo de que a proibição seria necessária para proteger a saúde da população, os consumidores e as famílias dos prejuízos causados pelas apostas.

“A MP seria um milagre, resolveria tudo!”, questionou a desembargadora, ao afirmar que a justificativa apresentada pelo governo não era suficiente para sustentar a medida.

O pedido da CDA Gaming havia sido negado por dois juízes na primeira instância. A empresa recorreu e conseguiu uma decisão favorável no TRF3.

A autorização é provisória e vale apenas para as três plataformas da empresa. A proibição continua em vigor para as demais casas de apostas.

A empresa CDA Gaming LTDA recebeu autorização do Ministério da Fazenda, por meio da portaria SPA/MF 255/25, para explorar apostas esportivas e jogos online, nas modalidades física e virtual, mediante pagamento de R$ 30 milhões.

O título tinha validade originalmente prevista até 31 de dezembro de 2029 e baseou o pedido feito à Justiça Federal para retomar as atividades.

Site do governo comunica o bloqueio de plataformas de apostas que operam no país. — Foto: Joédson Alves/Agência Brasil

O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) anunciou em 25 de setembro a proibição total de apostas de quota fixa no país, as chamadas bets. A vedação inclui também jogos online e cassinos virtuais no país, como por exemplo, o "Jogo do Tigrinho".

A proibição, feita a nove dias das eleições, foi formalizada em uma Medida Provisória (MP) assinada pelo presidente. A medida foi publicada em edição extra do Diário Oficial da União (DOU).

A Associação Nacional de Jogos e Loterias (ANJL) e o Instituto Brasileiro de Jogo Responsável (IBJR) protocolaram três dias depois, em 28 de setembro, um pedido no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) para suspender os efeitos da medida provisória de Lula que determinou a proibição imediata da exploração, oferta, intermediação e publicidade das bets e dos cassinos online no país.

As entidades argumentam que a MP foi publicada sem demonstração de urgência. E que o próprio Executivo havia enviado ao Congresso o projeto de lei que resultou no marco regulatório do setor de 2023, destacando, à época, os benefícios econômicos da legalização.

As associações pedem que o STF suspenda integralmente a MP até a deliberação definitiva da medida pelo Congresso ou até o julgamento de ações em curso na Corte, preservando a vigência da legislação anterior e o funcionamento das empresas autorizadas.

A audiência reuniu representantes dos clubes de futebol, entidades da sociedade civil e ministros do governo. As apostas esportivas foram legalizadas em 2018, mas a regulamentação só veio no fim de 2023. O governo arrecadou cerca de R$ 15 bilhões com a taxação das apostas.

Na audiência, o ministro Luiz Fux defendeu o banimento das bets, mas afirmou que a medida do governo trouxe questões que precisam ser discutidas pelo STF, como a segurança jurídica dos contratos e os impactos econômicos da proibição.

articles.title: The loo crew
articles.summary: It’s holiday season, not just on our roads, but also in the skies.
articles.body: It’s holiday season, not just on our roads, but also in the skies. And if sitting in bumper-to-bumper traffic is painful, sitting on a clogged toilet at 35,000 feet is a special kind of hell. Even if you’ve been spared the experience, you’ve almost certainly read horror stories about it, in media and social media. So, we have a suggestion for not just Tewolde Gebremariam, Air India’s new CEO, who this week made his first major public appearance, but all airline bosses. Speaking at Aviation India summit 2026, he underlined the airline’s big and long-term upgrade plans, to boost its international operations. But one thing that will lift the brand right away, is providing professional janitorial services for every long-haul flight.It might sound odd at first, but hear us out. Right now cabin crews are assigned the responsibility to inspect toilets. IATA guidance suggests they should do regular checks, typically every 20-30 minutes. But cabin crew are already taking care of meal services, mediating seat-recline disputes, occasionally managing misbehaving passengers, on top of all their safety duties. When airlines happily invest fortunes in lie-flat beds, mood lighting, and celebrity-chef menus, why leave the most basic human necessity to such a slapdash arrangement? Cabin crew, with many competing responsibilities, obviously cannot focus on maintaining the toilets well. And everything that they miss, translates into a very unpleasant flying experience for passengers, especially on a 6-16 hour flight. The only way to make sure this job is done properly, is to assign it to a specific person.It’s true that in India, cleaning toilets isn’t a socially neutral occupation, but comes with a lot of caste and class baggage. In many parts of the world, though, it’s just another job. In many modern Indian offices too, not to mention airports, it’s a job with plenty of applicants. Why would it be any different when airlines advertise the job, especially if it comes with good training and salary? A dedicated sanitation steward – we suggest this as a job title that’s both to-the-point and respectful – wouldn’t just keep things spotless. They would also gently educate passengers on what not to flush, before things go south in the loo.Last year, a Chicago-Delhi Air India flight was forced to turn around, after eight of its 12 toilets became “unserviceable”. Last month, a similar plumbing crisis forced a Madrid-Dallas American Airlines flight to divert to New York. And there are other such cases. What we are suggesting actually serves a global need. Sanitation management is not a priority for airlines, because it isn’t considered critical for airworthiness. But clean toilets are part of their most elemental duty of care, not some optional luxury. Do it before, as they say, sh*t hits the fan.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: Jude Law and several celebrities join residents to oppose a proposed London housing development; the 45-home project near Blackheath station faces objections over parking, local businesses and the area's character
articles.summary: A proposed housing development near Blackheath station in south-east London has drawn opposition from residents and prominent figures, including actor
articles.body: A proposed housing development near Blackheath station in south-east London has drawn opposition from residents and prominent figures, including actor Jude Law, Dominic Cooper, broadcaster Jools Holland and musician Manfred Mann. The plans, submitted by Acorn Property Group, would replace much of the station’s car park with 45 homes, raising concerns about parking, local businesses and the neighbourhood’s historic character. Campaigners argue that the scheme could disrupt Blackheath village’s community life, while Lewisham Council has postponed its decision to seek further information on the proposal and its potential effects.Jude Law and celebrities oppose the Blackheath housing developmentThe controversy centres on a site that currently serves commuters and hosts Blackheath Farmers’ Market every Sunday. Acorn Property Group’s proposal includes 20 terraced houses and 25 flats arranged across buildings ranging from three to five storeys. The development would significantly change the station car park and its role in the surrounding village.As reported by The Independent, the campaign against the project has attracted support from several well-known residents and people with longstanding connections to Blackheath. Jude Law, Dominic Cooper, Sarah Hadland, Nick Ferrari, Lucy Boynton, Katherine Parkinson and Kellie Shirley were among those who signed an open letter calling on Lewisham Council to reject the plans.The campaign has also drawn backing from musicians and public figures including Mark Knopfler, Manfred Mann, Glenn Tilbrook, Sir Terry Waite and Jim Moir, better known as Vic Reeves. Their objections reflect concerns that the proposed buildings would be out of proportion with the area and undermine its distinctive identity.Blackheath is a leafy neighbourhood known for independent cafes, bookshops and well-preserved Georgian and Victorian streets. The village is part of a conservation area designated in 1968, making it the first of its kind in London.How much parking would the Blackheath station development removeParking has become one of the most significant points of disagreement. According to TimeOut London, the existing station car park has 162 spaces, but the proposed development would leave only 17.Campaigners say the reduction could make it harder for shoppers to reach Blackheath's independent businesses, particularly at weekends. Residents have also raised concerns about additional traffic and congestion on roads already under pressure.People living along Collins Street, where two-storey terraced houses face the station car park, feared the development would bring disruption and affect their privacy. Some residents said they would consider moving if the plans were approved.The Greenwich Wire highlighted concerns from local traders about the consequences of losing parking. Nick Ellis of Ellis Butchers said the village depended on parking, particularly for weekend trade. Councillors also questioned whether the developer's parking assessment adequately reflected the area's busiest periods.One committee member pointed out that the parking survey had been conducted during the week rather than at weekends, when the village attracts more visitors. The debate has therefore extended beyond the number of spaces to whether the evidence accurately captures how people use Blackheath.The farmers’ market has become central to the disputeBlackheath Farmers’ Market is another major concern for opponents of the development. The market currently operates in the station car park every Sunday and attracts thousands of people to the village, supporting nearby shops and businesses.The campaign's open letter, published on the Reject Blackheath Station website, warns that the market could be squeezed into a narrow area under the proposed arrangement. Signatories argue that the loss of space and parking could threaten the market's future and reduce the number of customers visiting local businesses.The Greenwich Wire reported that councillor Amanda de Ryk questioned whether the market's proposed new layout would protect its long-term viability. She also raised concerns about the proximity of market stalls to the homes, suggesting that noise, footfall and clearing up could create tensions between residents and market operators.However, the market's management has taken a different position. The Greenwich Wire quoted London Farmers’ Markets director Mark Handley as saying the proposals would provide improved facilities, including a water supply for the first time and upgraded power. He argued that the company would not support a development that put the market at risk.This has created a disagreement between campaigners who fear the market will be damaged and its operator, which believes the redevelopment could improve its facilities.What does Acorn Property Group say about the proposed homesAcorn Property Group has defended the scheme as a way to make use of land that is primarily functioning as a station car park. The company says the proposal responds to London's urgent housing needs while following planning policies that encourage new homes.As reported by The Independent, Acorn described its approach as sustainable and heritage-led, arguing that the design would support residents and the natural environment. It also said consultation had taken place through in-person events and online engagement with residents, businesses and other stakeholders.The development would include 8 homes for people on Lewisham's housing waiting list, according to The Greenwich Wire. Supporters of the scheme have argued that the need for additional housing should not be overlooked in the debate over parking and building design.At the January 2026 planning meeting, resident Freddy Soames argued that the village needed more housing and should not prioritise parking spaces over 45 homes. His comments offered a counterpoint to the campaign, highlighting the difficulties of balancing local concerns with wider housing demand.What happens next after Lewisham Council defers its decisionThe Greenwich Wire reported that Lewisham Council received 1,202 objections to the development, compared with 30 comments in support.At its January 2026 meeting, Lewisham Council's planning committee deferred the decision after asking for further information about parking, the effect on local businesses, the farmers’ market and access for emergency services.A council spokesperson said the committee did not believe it had enough information to make a fully informed decision and wanted the local economy's interests properly considered.You use AI every day. articles.title: How deep is Pakistan's debt dependence on China? The numbers tell the story
articles.summary: Pakistan’s external debt has nearly doubled over the past decade, climbing to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $68.67 billion in 2015, according to a World
articles.body: Pakistan’s external debt has nearly doubled over the past decade, climbing to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $68.67 billion in 2015, according to a World Bank report cited by Dawn.The figures underline the Islamic country’s growing dependence on foreign borrowing to meet its financial needs.The debt stock comprised $107.07 billion in public and publicly guaranteed loans, $17.58 billion in private non-guaranteed debt and $10.45 billion in short-term borrowing.Of the public debt, multilateral institutions accounted for the largest share at $56.83 billion. Pakistan also owed $42.43 billion to bilateral lenders and $7.8 billion to private creditors.China remained Pakistan’s biggest individual creditor, with outstanding loans of $22.4 billion. The World Bank was next with $19.2 billion, followed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), to which Pakistan owed $16.83 billion.The report also highlighted the difference in borrowing costs. Loans from official creditors had an average maturity of 16 years, a four-year grace period and an interest rate of 3.6%. Private credit, in contrast, came at a much steeper average interest rate of 8.6%, with a repayment period of three years and a grace period of just one year.Across the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region, debt-service and interest ratios showed improvement.However, the region’s external debt-to-gross national income (GNI) ratio rose from 26.7% to 29.4% in 2025. This was the sharpest annual increase recorded by any region, pointing to a continued build-up of external debt.Pakistan also received some relief through fresh financing and loan extensions during the year. China extended the maturity of $2 billion in loans, while the International Monetary Fund (IMF) disbursed $2.3 billion under its Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility programmes, aimed at supporting the country’s longer-term economic stability.You use AI every day. articles.title: Macau pro-democracy activist Au Kam San sentenced To 12.5 years in jail
articles.summary: A prominent pro-democracy activist in Macau was sentenced to 12 years and six months in prison on Friday after being convicted of subversion and other
articles.body: A prominent pro-democracy activist in Macau was sentenced to 12 years and six months in prison on Friday after being convicted of subversion and other national security offences, marking the first known national security trial in the China-governed gambling enclave, local broadcaster TDM reported.Au Kam San, 69, was arrested in July 2025 on allegations of colluding with foreign forces to threaten national security. His trial was held behind closed doors on September 16 and 18, according to TDM.According to news agency Reuters, Au is among Macau's best-known democratic campaigners and served as a legislator in the former Portuguese colony for nearly 20 years. His court-appointed lawyer did not immediately respond to requests for comment.The sentencing came a day after prominent Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong, who became an internationally recognised figure during the financial hub's democracy movement, received a 10-year prison term on charges of colluding with foreign entities under Hong Kong's national security law.Macau's court of first instance found Au guilty of subverting state power, establishing connections with foreign organisations or individuals to carry out activities threatening national security, and violating secrecy provisions.Citing the court, TDM reported that although Au had no previous criminal record and admitted to a substantial part of the offences, the judges considered his intention to be particularly serious, with the unlawful nature of his actions and their potential consequences deemed extremely grave.However, the court cleared him of two other subversion charges, citing insufficient evidence.According to TDM, the combined sentencing range for the offences was between 11 years and three months and 19 years and six months. After considering the case, the court handed down a consolidated prison sentence of 12 years and six months.Over the years, Au had campaigned for democratic reforms and initiatives aimed at strengthening civil society in Macau, which was transferred from Portuguese to Chinese administration in 1999, two years after neighbouring Hong Kong returned to Chinese rule following the end of British colonial rule.Human Rights Watch criticised the proceedings, alleging violations of due process. The organisation said the sentence imposed by the Macau authorities sent a chilling warning to peaceful critics in the territory.Pro-democracy activists and public voices have faced mounting restrictions and a sustained crackdown across the Chinese-administered territories since Hong Kong's massive pro-democracy protests in 2019.In February, Hong Kong media tycoon Jimmy Lai, one of China's most prominent critics, was sentenced to 20 years in prison for collusion with foreign forces and sedition. His landmark trial also drew widespread international criticism.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Will be dealt with iron hand': SC issues contempt notice to Kerala Congress over controversial CJI post
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has issued a contempt notice to office-bearers of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) over a social media post
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has issued a contempt notice to office-bearers of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) over a social media post targeting Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, observing that freedom of expression cannot be used as a shield to interfere with the administration of justice.The apex court said, "Judgments are always open to criticism but freedom of expression can't be a shield for interference with administration of justice.""Any attempt to undermine authority of court needs to be dealt with iron hand," it further said, as cited by PTI.Reiterating the supremacy of the Constitution, the court added, "Constitution is supreme, no individual or political organisation stands above it."The Supreme Court has registered a petition based on a complaint seeking contempt proceedings against the KPCC over the social media post. According to the apex court's website, a complaint addressed to the CJI by advocate Vineet Jindal on October 13 was registered as a writ petition on October 30.The complaint also sought directions to authorities to ascertain whether a political demonstration and slogan-shouting held on the Supreme Court premises on the evening of October 12, 2026, involving Rahul Gandhi and other political leaders, took place without authorisation or caused any obstruction to the movement of advocates, litigants, judicial officers or court staff.A post targeting the CJI from the official Congress Kerala account on X went viral on October 12, drawing sharp criticism on social media, before being deleted. The party subsequently removed the person responsible for publishing it.In a statement, KPCC president Sunny Joseph said the person responsible for posting the controversial message on the party's official X account had been removed from the charge. He clarified that the post was made without the knowledge, consent or consultation of the KPCC leadership.Joseph also said the Congress party had no disagreement with regard to the impartiality of the judiciary.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: OBC creamy layer row: SC protects past jobs, promotions but leaves pending cases open
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday clarified that its March 11 ruling on determining the creamy layer status of Other Backward Class (OBC) candidates
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday clarified that its March 11 ruling on determining the creamy layer status of Other Backward Class (OBC) candidates would not reopen completed appointments, promotions or seniority positions.The top court said cases that are still pending would be examined individually by the courts, based on their merits and the candidates' eligibility.A bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice R Mahadevan delivered the ruling while hearing an application filed by the Centre seeking clarity on how the March 11 judgment should be implemented. The Court also extended the deadline for compliance with its earlier directions by eight weeks.The clarification comes after the Centre raised concerns that applying the March 11 ruling retrospectively could unsettle years of government recruitments, service allocations and admissions to educational institutions.Centre flags concerns over past recruitmentsIn its application, the government argued that applying the revised interpretation to past cases could affect appointments and admissions made under the rules and eligibility criteria in force at the time. It warned that this could create uncertainty over OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression.“Retrospective or belated application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the relevant time and may create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression. It may also affect admissions to Central and State educational institutions, universities and professional institutions. The Applicant therefore respectfully submits that the temporal operation of the Judgment requires clarification so as to avoid unsettling completed selections, appointments and admissions and the consequential rights arising therefrom”, the plea stated as per LiveLaw.The Centre said more than 5.69 lakh reserved vacancies, including 3.70 lakh OBC vacancies, were filled in Central government ministries, departments and their subordinate offices between 2016 and 2025.These recruitments were conducted under the August 8, 1993 Office Memorandum and subsequent government instructions.It argued that retrospective implementation could also necessitate a review of service allocations made through Civil Services Examinations since 2012. This could potentially lead to changes in the services and cadres allotted to officers already in government service, affecting their seniority and promotion prospects.The government also flagged possible complications in recruitment examinations conducted by the Railways, banks, Department of Posts and paramilitary organisations. It said similar disputes could arise in 18 States and Union Territories that follow the 1993 guidelines.The Centre further pointed out that candidates who become eligible for technical services several years after an examination might no longer meet the prescribed physical and medical standards. It also warned that reopening admissions granted to lakhs of students in universities and professional institutions could create difficulties, particularly where there are no provisions for additional seats.Dispute over salary-based creamy layer criteriaThe clarification application stems from the Supreme Court's March 11 judgment on how the creamy layer among OBC candidates should be identified.The Court had ruled that a parent's salary alone cannot be used to determine whether an OBC candidate belongs to the creamy layer. The nature and category of the post held by the parents must also be taken into account.The dispute centred on two government instructions, the Office Memorandum issued on August 8, 1993, and a subsequent clarification dated October 14, 2004.The 1993 memorandum laid down the criteria for identifying the OBC creamy layer. It did not make a parent's salary the sole basis for exclusion from reservation benefits. Under the applicable Income/Wealth Test, salary and agricultural income are excluded from the income calculation, while the status and category of the parent's post remain relevant under the prescribed criteria.The 2004 clarification dealt with employees working in organisations such as public sector undertakings (PSUs), banks, universities and private companies, where the equivalence of their posts with government positions had not been established. It provided for consideration of parents' salary income in such cases.The Supreme Court held that the 2004 clarification could not introduce a new condition that was not part of the original 1993 policy. It also observed that treating children of PSU and private-sector employees differently from those of similarly placed government employees could amount to hostile discrimination and violate Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution, which guarantee equality before the law and equal opportunity in public employment.Centre seeks time to frame uniform mechanismThe government has maintained that it is not challenging or seeking a review of the March 11 judgment. Instead, it wants clarity on when the ruling should apply and how its directions should be implemented.The Centre has sought two years to consult stakeholders, establish equivalence between posts in non-government organisations and government positions, and develop a uniform mechanism for determining creamy-layer status in cases where such equivalence has not been established.It has also asked the SC not to disturb completed selections, appointments, service and cadre allocations, seniority positions and admissions made under the eligibility rules applicable at the time. The government has separately sought clarity on candidates who were already participating in examinations or recruitment processes when the March 11 judgment was delivered.In a separate interim application, the Centre sought permission to proceed with service allocation for 958 candidates recommended by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in the Civil Services Examination 2025, using the existing 1993 framework while the clarification application remained pending.The government argued that any further delay would push back the candidates' Foundation Course, training and induction schedules. It said the resulting disruption could not be reversed even if the Court eventually accepted its position.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Two years after Donald Trump's conviction on 34 felony counts over a $130,000 payment to Stormy Daniels, his lawyers ask a New York appeals court to overturn the verdict on immunity and legal grounds
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump is once again under judicial scrutiny.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump is once again under judicial scrutiny. Nearly two years after a New York jury found him guilty of 34 felony counts connected to a hush money payment made before the 2016 presidential election, Trump's legal team is attempting to have the historic verdict overturned. The latest challenge brought the President's lawyers face to face with a five-judge appeals panel, which closely examined questions surrounding presidential immunity, election laws and the evidence presented during his trial.Lawyers challenge the legal foundation of the convictionAccording to AP News, Trump's attorneys appeared before a New York appellate court on Thursday, November 5, arguing that the conviction should be overturned because the prosecution relied on federal election law to elevate the charges from misdemeanours to felonies.The case originated from a $130,000 payment made by Trump's former lawyer and fixer, Michael Cohen, to adult film performer Stormy Daniels shortly before the 2016 election. The payment was intended to secure her silence about an alleged sexual encounter with Trump approximately a decade earlier, which the president has consistently denied.Cohen was subsequently reimbursed by Trump's company in 2017, with the payments recorded as legal expenses. Prosecutors argued that the business records were deliberately falsified to conceal an alleged conspiracy to influence the election.Trump's lawyer Robert Giuffra Jr. maintained that Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg's office had improperly relied on the Federal Election Campaign Act (FECA), arguing that federal election law could not form the basis of a state prosecution.CBS News reported that the defence also challenged the jury instructions, arguing that jurors should have been required to unanimously agree on the underlying crime that elevated the falsification charges to felonies.Presidential immunity becomes another battlegroundAnother significant aspect of the appeal concerns evidence from Trump's first presidential term. His legal team argued that testimony involving former White House communications director Hope Hicks and Trump's social media posts should not have been presented to jurors because they involved official presidential conduct protected by immunity.Hicks had testified about discussions with Trump after the Daniels allegations became public in 2018. His lawyers maintained that the conversations concerned his responsibilities as president, including managing press inquiries.However, prosecutors disputed that interpretation. According to AP News, Steven Wu, representing Bragg's office, argued that the conversations reflected Trump's personal opinions rather than official presidential duties.The prosecution also maintained that even if certain evidence should have been excluded, its admission did not affect the overall outcome because substantial other evidence supported the conviction.Judges question both sides as Trump continues his fightThe five-judge panel repeatedly interrupted both legal teams with questions about their arguments. One judge also questioned whether the cumulative admission of potentially improper evidence could still be considered harmless.CBS News noted that Trump's defence additionally challenged the requirement for jury unanimity on the underlying offences, while prosecutors pointed out that the trial defence had previously accepted the judge's approach.The May 2024 conviction followed a unanimous jury verdict. Trump was found guilty on all 34 counts but received no punishment that impeded his return to the White House.His attempts to shift the case from state to federal court meanwhile have also faced setbacks.A federal judge denied his immunity dismissal request for the third time in August, with another appeal scheduled for Nov. 16.The New York appeals court has not announced its decision, leaving Trump's historic conviction in limbo.Images Courtesy: istock and InstagramYou use AI every day. articles.title: Australian holiday accommodation advertised for up to A$450 a night after a shipping container conversion draws neighbour complaints over lighting and alleged unauthorised development
articles.summary: Clifftop at Hepburn, a luxury holiday villa near Hepburn Springs in central Victoria, was advertised for up to A$450 a night after the business added a
articles.body: Clifftop at Hepburn, a luxury holiday villa near Hepburn Springs in central Victoria, was advertised for up to A$450 a night after the business added a converted shipping container and other structures that the local council says required a planning permit. Neighbours complained about intrusive lighting and signage, and council inspectors recorded in early 2024 potential breaches including extra dwellings built without planning and building approvals. The site lies in a bushfire-prone area. The business insists its operations are lawful and that it never defied the planning scheme, and the dispute has played out across a tribunal and the Supreme Court.African-themed stays with sweeping views, from a shipping container to a converted train carriageAccording to ABC News, the accommodation site overlooking the town of Hepburn Springs offers sweeping views of the central Victorian countryside, with names such as Zulu, Sahara and Serengeti. The business running it features in Qantas’s points program. Known as the Sahara villas, the site has been run by Clifftop at Hepburn since August 2022. Jumanji, understood to be among the new structures, is a converted shipping container with an adjoining pergola advertised for about A$300 a night. Eaglesnest, a one-bedroom villa advertised at the higher price, appears to have been installed in 2023.Neighbours in a sleepy region complained about lighting and signage as new structures appearedIn the months after Clifftop at Hepburn took over the site, neighbours were unhappy as new structures, lights and business signage allegedly began to appear. One complained to the council that an illuminated sign left the property “lit up like Luna Park”. Satellite images from November 2022 and January 2026 show new structures beyond the main residence, garage and three detached cottages first built there.The business’s social media posts also antagonised council figures and occasionally neighbours. One 2023 post, showing apparent works, predicted that nosy neighbours would soon complain and told the council that no permit was required.Council inspectors found extra units, a garage conversion and vegetation removal, documents showDocuments released under Freedom of Information laws show the site is covered by bushfire and environmental overlays, planning tools that can bring stricter rules for development in sensitive areas. When council staff inspected, they identified extensive additional works, two more accommodation units, a garage converted into accommodation, and a bus and a train being converted. An internal email from early 2024 also listed non-compliance with endorsed plans, signage, lighting and vegetation removal.The council took steps to resolve the issues, endorsing the converted garage, known as Safari, and some signage through secondary consent, a streamlined pathway generally used for minor changes.A refused retrospective application led to a tribunal case and a Supreme Court challengeIn a 2025 social media post, the business suggested Eaglesnest went up without council approval. It said it built the villa after concluding the council would never approve one, relying on its right to register the site as a caravan park. In 2025, it also lodged a planning application seeking retrospective endorsement of the new structures and proposing a handful of yurts and glamping domes. It asked for approval through secondary consent, arguing that case law supported this and that the original permit allowed the whole lot to operate as a tourist establishment. A planning barrister engaged by the council advised that a tribunal would probably agree the whole site could be used for tourism, but that planning permission would still be needed for additional buildings and works.The council refused the application in August 2025, saying secondary consent could not be used and that registering the site as a caravan park did not remove the need for a planning permit. David Penman, the business’s co-owner, told ABC News that the registration significantly relaxed the requirements for the structures, which he says are properly described as moveable dwellings.The refusal led the business to bring a case in the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal, which was paused so it could ask the Supreme Court to quash the refusal, alleging the decision was biased. Penman told the Supreme Court in an affidavit that the threat of enforcement and legal costs of many tens of thousands of dollars forced construction to stop and three full-time workers to be laid off.Bushfire safety in a very high-risk area, an independent assessment meets neighbours’ concernsNeighbour Linda Hancock, who is seeking to be joined to the tribunal case, told the broadcaster she was evacuated from her property for four days during the 2019 bushfire season, when the whole of Hepburn was threatened. She said the site sits in a bushfire management overlay area, where planning and construction rules exist to protect people staying there.Neighbours point to an earlier glamping application by the business for nearby land. The tribunal eventually granted it on a second appeal, with a more sophisticated bushfire safety plan, but restricted its operation because of the area’s very high bushfire risk.Penman argues the risk at the Sahara Villas site has been properly assessed, first by the Country Fire Authority for the site’s initial permit, then in an independent assessment submitted with the caravan park application, which he says finds the site safe. He declined to give further details of that assessment. In tribunal filings, he said a further Country Fire Authority assessment through a buildings and works process would be an excessive third assessment.Private prosecutions left the council without a quorum, and Victoria plans to change the lawEarlier in 2026, Penman launched private prosecutions against four Hepburn Shire councillors, the mayor and the council’s then chief executive. Because councillors must stand down when charged, the council was left without a quorum to make decisions until the charges were dropped. The Office of Public Prosecutions reviewed a large volume of material from Penman and found no reasonable prospect of conviction, and he was reportedly ordered to pay the defendants’ legal costs.In the same statement, Penman said the prosecutions concerned alleged conduct and evidence in their own right and were not brought as leverage in the planning dispute. The council described the move as a deliberate manipulation of local government laws. Planned changes to Victorian law would require councillors to stand down only when charges are brought by a law enforcement body.A second Supreme Court case, launched in January against the council, its former chief executive, its longest-serving councillor and a planning officer over separate decisions, remained live. The defendants pushed for it to be dismissed, but a barrister appointed by Penman was given the chance to amend it.The council says a planning permit application would let neighbours and public agencies objectIn a statement, the council said it had advised the business how to legalise structures it described as illegally built before an application was lodged under the incorrect secondary consent pathway. It said the structures cannot be treated as minor administrative changes, and that the correct route is a planning permit application. That would trigger a formal referral notifying neighbours, the Country Fire Authority and water authorities, giving them the chance to record concerns or objections. The planning-related Supreme Court case was vacated before a trial was due to begin in late August, and the tribunal case remained before the tribunal at the time of reporting.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1990, a cockpit window blew out at 17,300 feet and sucked British Airways captain Tim Lancaster halfway out of his plane; crew members held his legs for about 20 minutes until the jet landed and he survived
articles.summary: A British Airways captain was nearly pulled out of his aircraft after a cockpit window shattered at 24,000 feet during a flight from England to Spain in
articles.body: A British Airways captain was nearly pulled out of his aircraft after a cockpit window shattered at 24,000 feet during a flight from England to Spain in June 1990. As the aircraft lost pressure, the force pulled the pilot's upper body through the broken window. Two crew members held on to him while the co-pilot took control and prepared for an emergency landing.According to Associated Press' then report, the incident took place on June 10, 1990, aboard British Airways flight 5390. The BAC-111 aircraft had taken off from Birmingham and was heading to Malaga, Spain, with 81 passengers and six crew members on board. Captain Tim Lancaster, 41, was flying the aircraft with co-pilot Alistair Atchison, 39.About 20 minutes after take-off, a cockpit window shattered. The sudden loss of pressure affected the flight deck and pulled Lancaster out of his seat. His head and shoulders were outside the aircraft, leaving the crew with little time to react.A steward in the forward galley heard a loud bang and saw what had happened. He rushed towards the cockpit and managed to grab Lancaster's legs. Another steward, Simon Rogers, joined him and helped restrain the captain. Their efforts prevented Lancaster from being pulled completely out of the aircraft.Meanwhile, Atchison took control of the aircraft and made an emergency call. He turned the plane around and prepared to land at Southampton Airport. The aircraft landed safely at around 9 am, ending an emergency that had put the captain's life at risk.Crew responded quicklyA British Airways spokesman described the crew's response to the incident in comments reported by United Press International."One of the cabin crew went straight to the flight deck, where he managed to grab ahold of the captain, whose head and shoulders I believe were out the window," the spokesman said.He also explained how another steward helped hold Lancaster while the co-pilot concentrated on landing the aircraft. "A second steward, Simon Rogers, strapped himself into the captain's seat and restrained the captain while the first officer undertook the landing," he said.The co-pilot, Atchison, radioed a Mayday message to Eastleigh Airport in Southampton. He then brought the aircraft down safely. Southampton was about 76 miles south-west of London, according to the UPI report.The emergency landing allowed the passengers and crew to leave the aircraft safely. However, the incident had left several people shaken.Pilot suffered fractures and frostbiteLancaster was taken to Southampton Hospital for treatment. He was listed in comfortable condition, according to the British Airways spokesman quoted by UPI.His injuries included fractures to his elbow, wrist and thumb. He also suffered frostbite to one hand and shock.The sudden loss of pressure in the cockpit had not affected the passenger cabin in the same way. However, six passengers and crew members were treated for shock and later released from hospital, UPI reported.British Airways arranged another aircraft for the passengers who wanted to continue their journey. Seventy-seven passengers travelled onwards to Malaga.The incident raised questions about what had caused the cockpit window to break during the flight. British Airways officials said they did not immediately know why the windscreen had shattered. Civil aviation investigators began examining the aircraft to establish the cause.You use AI every day.
