articles.body: 3M has agreed to commit up to $7.35 billion over nine years to resolve personal injury claims linked to PFAS contamination, in what is being described as a landmark settlement in the United States. The agreement, announced in a 3M press release and reported by the Associated Press, could provide compensation to as many as 120,000 people who say exposure to contaminated water harmed their health. The settlement does not admit wrongdoing by 3M. Instead, it establishes a structured framework for resolving claims from individuals who allege that PFAS, often called “forever chemicals,” contributed to serious health conditions after exposure through contaminated drinking water or other sources. Read more about it here:What the settlement coversThe agreement is designed to address individual personal injury claims rather than the broader public-water-system contamination cases that have already resulted in separate settlements. It applies to people who allege PFAS-related injuries and meet the eligibility requirements set out in the settlement framework.Under the terms, 3M will commit up to $7.35 billion over nine years. The money is intended to fund compensation for eligible claimants, with the final amount dependent on the number of valid claims and the outcome of the claims process.The settlement includes a wide range of potential claimants, with some reports estimating that as many as 120,000 people may qualify. That scale makes it one of the most significant PFAS-related personal injury settlements in the country.Why does PFAS matter?Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, or PFAS, are a family of synthetic chemicals used for decades in a wide variety of products and processes, from nonstick cookware and water-resistant clothing to firefighting foam and industrial applications. They are known to be resistant to breakdown in the environment and in the human body, earning them the nickname “forever chemicals.”Researchers and regulators have connected exposure to a variety of health risks, raising concerns about PFAS. These include some cancers, liver and thyroid problems, immune-system effects and developmental problems, although individual claims still depend on the facts of each case.Contamination has been most severe in neighborhoods near industrial sites, military bases and places where firefighting foam was used. In many of these places, residents say PFAS entered groundwater and drinking-water supplies, creating long-term exposure risks.A structured claims processThe settlement creates a structured process for evaluating and paying eligible claims. Rather than leaving each case to be litigated individually, the framework is intended to provide a more predictable path for people seeking compensation.Claimants will need to provide documentation and meet the eligibility criteria that are set out in the agreement. The process is expected to involve medical and exposure evidence and payments will be determined by the severity and type of injury alleged.The nine-year payment schedule gives 3M time to spread out the financial commitment. It also gives claimants a defined timeline for when compensation may become available, although individual payouts will still depend on the review process.What 3M has saidIn its announcement, 3M described the agreement as a way to bring certainty and resolution to a complex set of claims. The company has said the settlement does not constitute an admission of liability or wrongdoing.3M has faced mounting legal pressure over PFAS in recent years, with thousands of lawsuits filed by individuals, municipalities and other entities. The company has already reached separate agreements related to public water systems, making this new settlement another major step in its broader effort to manage PFAS-related litigation.The company has also said it is continuing to invest in remediation and in developing alternatives to PFAS in its products. Those efforts are part of a wider corporate response to the regulatory and legal challenges posed by the chemicals.What it means for claimantsFor people who believe they were harmed by PFAS exposure, the settlement represents a potential route to compensation without going through a full trial. It also signals growing recognition that individual health claims deserve a structured response, not just case-by-case litigation.The size of the fund, up to $7.35 billion, reflects both the seriousness of the allegations and the number of people potentially affected. It also points to how PFAS contamination has gone from being a niche environmental problem to a significant public health and legal issue.Claimants will still have to negotiate the eligibility and documentation requirements, but a defined framework may make the process more accessible than just filing a lawsuit. Legal representatives and claimant groups are expected to play a key role in helping people understand their options.A landmark momentThe settlement is being called landmark because of its size, its scope and the way it addresses individual injury claims rather than just municipal water systems. It marks a significant shift in how PFAS litigation is being handled in the United States.While the agreement may not reverse the health impacts already experienced, it could provide some financial relief to communities affected by contamination.It’s a major step for 3M in addressing one of the most consequential legal challenges facing the company.As the claims process moves forward, attention will turn to how many people come forward, how claims are evaluated and how quickly compensation is distributed. Those details will determine whether the settlement delivers on its promise of meaningful relief for the people at the centre of the PFAS crisis.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In California, Arnold Alois Schwarzenegger laid bricks while bodybuilding, then built a masonry business; he later became an actor and governor
articles.summary: Discover the inspiring journey of Arnold Schwarzenegger, from his humble beginnings as a bricklayer and bodybuilder to becoming a Hollywood icon and California's 38th governor. Learn how he navigated challenges and transformed his life through entrepreneurship and politics.
articles.body: Before Arnold Schwarzenegger became an internationally recognised and well-loved Hollywood star and California’s 38th governor, he was earning his living through construction work. During this time, he was also pursuing competitive bodybuilding. In 1968, after he moved to the United States, the Austrian-born athlete began looking for ways to support himself in the foreign country where bodybuilding offered comparatively little reward. Schwarzenegger’s friendship with Franco Columbu, who was a fellow bodybuilder, eventually led him to a small bricklaying and masonry business in California. Initially, the duo reportedly took on residential construction and repair jobs. But an earthquake in 1971 brought an increase in demand, and the business later became an important part of Schwarzenegger’s journey, alongside bodybuilding exhibitions, fitness-related sales and subsequent real estate development.Journey from bodybuilding competitions to bricklayingBorn in Thal, Austria, Schwarzenegger developed an interest in bodybuilding when he was a teenager. At 20, he became the youngest winner of the Mr Universe title at the time, thus establishing himself as a promising athlete. In 1968, when he was 21, he moved to the US and settled in the Los Angeles area to pursue a further bodybuilding career. Competitive bodybuilding, however, did not offer the same financial rewards associated with the sport today. According to reports, even successful competitors had to find additional income to cover their living expenses.Schwarzenegger later brought Italian bodybuilder Franco Columbu with him to America with help from bodybuilding entrepreneur Joe Weider. Columbu had previously developed bricklaying skills in Italy and Germany. Schwarzenegger later, in an interview with author Tim Ferriss in 2018, shared that Columbu’s construction experience gave them an opportunity to earn money outside bodybuilding. The former California governor shared that, as they both were not making much from bodybuilding competitions, they decided to establish a small masonry business and accepted residential jobs.The duo started by building and repairing walls, patios, fireplaces and other structures at people’s homes. Schwarzenegger participated in the work and handled business responsibilities such as measurements, estimates, negotiations and customer interactions, while Columbu brought in the professional masonry experience. The pair had also devised a marketing strategy that would distinguish them from other contractors. In the interview with Tim Ferriss, Schwarzenegger recalled that they had advertised in the Los Angeles Times as European bricklayers and masonry experts, promoting European-style fireplaces and chimneys. This strategy helped them to gain interest from the public, especially at a time when European craftsmanship had gained commercial appeal in the United States.The 1971 earthquake expanded the businessOn February 9, 1971, the San Fernando earthquake, which is also known as the Sylmar earthquake, struck Southern California. The earthquake damaged buildings and infrastructure. The bodybuilder recalled that their company began receiving hundreds of calls on the telephone from people seeking estimates for damaged chimneys, walls, fireplaces and patios. To manage the additional workload, they recruited other bodybuilders from their gym. In the interview, Schwarzenegger shared that they employed 16 different bodybuilders across several construction jobs during the business’s operation. The recruited workers helped the partners complete repair and rebuild projects while continuing to train for bodybuilding competitions.His earlier construction work, however, faced a complication. During Schwarzenegger’s 2003 campaign for California governor, questions arose over whether or not his bricklaying activities were consistent with his immigration status before he became a permanent US citizen in 1974. A Los Angeles Times report, published in September 2003, noted that his earlier visas permitted him to work as an athlete rather than take ordinary employment. His campaign representatives defended his activities. Nevertheless, the controversy became part of the public discussion surrounding his early business history.Venturing into acting, business investments and public serviceSchwarzenegger did not limit himself to the bricklaying business. He also developed a mail-order business selling fitness-related products and instructional material, thus using his growing popularity in bodybuilding to attract customers. His bodybuilding gigs alongside his construction earnings, seminars and mail-order activities helped him accumulate savings. In the 2018 interview, he shared that he had saved around $27,000 by 1974. He later borrowed another $10,000 from bodybuilding entrepreneur Joe Weider for the down payment on a six-unit apartment building in Santa Monica.According to Schwarzenegger, the building was sold around two and a half years later for $365,000. He reinvested the proceeds in larger apartment buildings and expanded into other property ventures. On the other hand, his acting career had actually started before the expansion of the bricklaying business. The Austrian-born actor made his feature-film debut in Hercules in New York in 1970. He had debuted originally under the name Arnold Strong. He later received a Golden Globe for New Male Star of the Year for his role in Stay Hungry. Conan the Barbarian became his major international breakthrough, which was followed by James Cameron’s The Terminator in 1984. These films solidified his place in the Hollywood industry, making him one of the most recognised stars internationally.Schwarzenegger eventually moved from the entertainment industry and started a career in politics. In 2003, he entered California politics and won the gubernatorial recall election that removed incumbent Governor Gray Davis from office. He was sworn in as the state’s 38th governor on November 17, 2003, and served until January 3, 2011. The Global Warming Solutions Act of 2006 was one of the most notable laws signed during his administration. This act targets reducing California’s greenhouse gas emissions. Schwarzenegger’s early experience in California, therefore, was shaped both by athletic ambition and entrepreneurship.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In June 2023, Jessica Vincent paid $3.99 for a colourful vase at a Virginia Goodwill; six months later, a Carlo Scarpa piece sold for $107,100, earning her about $83,500
articles.summary: In an astounding tale, Jessica Vincent discovered a Carlo Scarpa vase at a Virginia Goodwill for just $3.99. After expert authentication, the vase sold for $107,100 at auction, revealing the hidden treasures that thrift shopping can uncover.
articles.body: A routine shopping excursion through a secondhand retail store led to the authentication of an old masterpiece. A small mark on the base sent Jessica Vincent looking beyond the price tag. The bottle-shaped glass vessel had no price displayed when she found it at a Goodwill shop in Hanover County, Virginia. According to The New York Times, she had set herself a ceiling of about $8.99, but the cashier said $3.99. She assumed the vase would’ve been worth around $1,000 or $2,000, but had not identified its maker.Vincent, at the time 43 years of age, visited the shop in June after training horses. The vase stood among the household goods. Amethyst and aqua bands appeared to move through its glass. What caught her attention was the letter “M” written on its base, which she took as a possible reference to Murano.She had years of experience searching for items in second-hand shops, having gone thrifting with her mother since childhood, as per the Associated Press report in 2023. Vincent was an avid Antiques Roadshow fan and researched purchases. Her earlier finds included a Balinese woodcarving and lithographs by Burt Groedel, which she believed were worth a few thousand dollars each. Along with her partner, Acosta, she visited thrift shops several times a week. They trained polo, sport and trail horses for work.Authenticating the vase, from its purchase to attributionExperience gave her an edge, but she needed proof of what she had found. Vincent, in order to be sure from her home, posted photographs of the vase in online glass-identification groups on Facebook. The responses from members suggested the design resembled work by Carlo Scarpa and advised her to go to Wright Auction House. This prompted her to contact the auction house for an expert assessment.Richard Wright, president of the auction house, recognised the design from her photograph and arranged for the vase’s examination. Wright sent two Italian glass specialists to Virginia to check out its authenticity. Vincent brought the vase out wrapped in bubble wrap and a tablecloth. She recalled their excitement when they first saw it: “It was incredible to have experts who handle very important pieces of glass who were very excited for my little thrift-store vase.”After examination, the vase was linked to Scarpa’s Pennellate series, made for an Italian glass company called Venini in 1942. Pennellate, in Italian, translates to brushstrokes. Following Wright’s account, the process involved applying coloured opaque glass to a vessel as it was blown, leaving marks that gave the impression of paint strokes. The glassblower had to keep rotating the vase while the colours were added. Scarpa’s drawings had to be translated into a physical object by the person working on the glass.The process was pedantic; as a result, only a small number of pieces were known to have been made. Wright said the auction house was cognizant of one other vase with the same shape and colour combination, which was held in a private collection. Vincent’s vase had no chips or cracks. This was an important highlight because even a chip, no matter how small it was, could drag the value below $10,000.The auction and what ensued after Initially, the Wright Auction House estimated the vase would sell for $30,000 to $50,000, according to the New York Times. It went under the hammer on 13 December 2023 and sold for $107,100. The buyer was a private collector and, following their request, remained anonymous. Vincent received about $83,500, with approximately $23,600 going to the auction house.Vincent decided not to keep the vase after finding out its rarity and value. Her reasoning was rather simple: keeping such a valuable item in the house meant exposing it to break-ins. She said to The New York Times that she wanted the piece restored to the art world because its existence had been unrecognised, and she hoped it would eventually be placed in a museum.The money was kept aside for a farmhouse Vincent had bought in January. The farmhouse was built in 1930 and required major renovation; at the time it was being heated with two space heaters. Her plans then included the installation of a heating and air-conditioning system, alongside a dishwasher and fencing.How the vase ended up at Goodwill remains unknown. Laura Faison, a spokeswoman for the Goodwill of Central and Coastal Virginia, said the organisation oversaw more than 2 million donations a year, making it impossible to identify the donor. As per the account of the Associated Press, the vase might have been on the shelf for a couple of days, given the volume of stock moving through stores. Faison said the vase might have come from someone clearing out a relative’s home.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Steven Curtis Chapman and his wife started Show Hope in 2003 hoping to help 100 children find families; 23 years later, their adoption grants have helped more than 10,000 children across 65 countries
articles.summary: Christian music star Steven Curtis Chapman and his wife, Mary Beth, have reached a major milestone with their non-profit organisation, Show Hope.
articles.body: Christian music star Steven Curtis Chapman and his wife, Mary Beth, have reached a major milestone with their non-profit organisation, Show Hope. The charity's adoption grants have now helped more than 10,000 children across 65 countries find permanent families. The couple started the organisation in 2003 with a simple goal of helping 100 children find loving homes. Twenty-three years later, Show Hope has gone far beyond what they first hoped to achieve. According to announcements published by JubileeCast and the Gospel Music Association, the milestone comes alongside a new song release from Chapman titled "10,000 Reasons/Greater Things". The song is scheduled to be released on Friday, 7 November 2026. It brings together the well-known worship song with Chapman's thanks for the families supported by the charity over the past two decades.Milestone linked to musical release and Nashville benefitTo celebrate helping 10,000 children and mark National Adoption Month, the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville is hosting a special benefit concert. The event will feature Chapman, country music star Carrie Underwood, Bill Anderson, and Louis York. As reported by Williamson Source, five dollars from every ticket sold for the Opry performances will go directly to Show Hope. The money will help support the organisation's ongoing grant programmes. The partnership is especially meaningful to Chapman. He grew up listening to the Grand Ole Opry on WSM radio, long before he became an official member of the famous music venue."The Grand Ole Opry has been a very special part of my story since I was a boy listening to WSM radio, and it played a pivotal role in launching my career as a performer," Chapman said in an official statement released before the event. "To now be a member of the Opry family and to partner for a special night celebrating something so close to Mary Beth's and my hearts, the miracle of adoption and the work of Show Hope, is an incredible honor."Two decades of removing financial barriersThe Chapmans founded Show Hope in 2003 after going through adoption themselves. Their family has six children, including three daughters who joined them through international adoption. The organisation mainly works to reduce the high costs that often stop families from completing the adoption process. Through its main Adoption Aid grant programme, Show Hope provides direct financial support to help cover adoption agency fees, legal expenses, and international travel costs. Over the past two decades, the non-profit has also expanded its work beyond financial support for adoption. It now offers Medical Care grants to help families looking after children with complex medical needs. In a public message to supporters, Chapman reflected on the milestone and thanked the donors who have helped keep the organisation running for more than two decades. "Only God could have written a story like this," Chapman shared in a statement published by JubileeCast. "Thank you to everyone who has prayed, given, and helped make this possible. We have 10,000 reasons to give thanks, and I believe the best is still ahead!"Opry partnership highlights national awareness effortThe benefit concert at the Grand Ole Opry is part of wider efforts to raise awareness about child welfare and adoption throughout November. Show Hope continues to accept and review grant applications from families in the United States and other countries. Its main goal remains to remove financial barriers and help children waiting for permanent families find loving homes. Tickets for the special benefit evening at the Grand Ole Opry House are still available through the venue's official ticketing system. Money raised through the event will go directly to Show Hope's Adoption Aid fund.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: At 23, Lee Su-jin cleaned rooms at a South Korean love hotel for a paycheck and a bed; the hotel review website he later turned into Yanolja was valued at $6.7 billion in 2021
articles.summary: Discover the inspiring story of Lee Su-jin who transitioned from cleaning rooms in a South Korean love hotel to founding Yanolja, a company valued at $6.7 billion. Learn about the journey, challenges, and transformation of the motel industry in South Korea.
articles.body: Lee Su-jin was 23 when he started cleaning rooms at a love hotel in South Korea. This job provided him with a regular income and accommodation, which helped him meet his living needs after losing his parents at a young age, according to CNBC in 2019. Most of the work involved changing beds for couples who had paid for a couple of hours of privacy, Malay Mail reported in 2017. Yanolja, the application identified, raised $1.7 billion in funding from the Vision Fund 2 of SoftBank in 2021. StartupIntros recorded the post-money valuation at $6.7 billion, although some media outlets reported a higher figure. In between these two events, lies the crackdown by the law on South Korea's motel industry, along with Lee’s gamble with selling a motel as a bright room.A 2004 crackdown thinned out the motel tradeThe hotel industry in South Korea flourished in the late 1990s and early 2000s due to a large number of permits issued by the government after the 1988 Seoul Olympics, according to Korea JoongAng Daily. Love hotels were also involved in prostitution, which is a criminal activity in the country. A Reuters report from August 2015 on South Korea’s love hotels said a 2004 crackdown under then President Roh Moo-hyun put many of them out of business. A study in PLOS ONE, Effects of implementing the act of prohibition on sex trafficking on female sex workers’ sexually transmitted infections, dates the Act’s implementation to 2005 and describes how prostitution blocks became contested ground between police and workers while they were being demolished after the Act came into force in September 2004, according to AFP.Lee began with a review platform in 2005 and launched Yanolja Lee founded a hotel review website, although the exact founding year remains unclear because of the reported timeline conflict. It later became an advertising site where owners tried to lure customers, according to CNBC’s 2019 article. Yanolja evolved to become a booking site in 2007. The appeal he made to newly married couples and travellers was that staying in such hotels would be secure and economical. Bloomberg interviewed Lee, then 39, at his Gangnam office in 2017. Lee Su-jin told Bloomberg in 2017, “If all the motels relied on love, they’d starve to death.”A Hotelinn executive said modernised motels could double or triple revenueThe transformation that Lee was selling became apparent by 2015. The article in Reuters spoke about the transformation from dirty windows and red lights in bedrooms being replaced with clean rooms fit for family use. According to the 30-year-old student, with the surname Yang, speaking with the agency, the couple comes to short-stay hotels together up to 4 times a month and such hotels have become common places where couples go on dates. Lee Seung-rae, the CEO of HotelInn, the company that gives management lessons to the owners of motels, told the agency that owners get double and even triple their income when they modernise their properties. He also mentioned that small and medium motels cannot earn anything from the overnight stay.Demand had a practical side too. Reporting from The World, a PRX programme, says that in a country with a severe housing shortage, these motels increasingly give privacy to young adults who live with their parents.SoftBank invested $1.7 billionMoney came later. On 15 July 2021, the company confirmed that the Vision Fund 2 invested $1.7 billion. The fund acquired an approximately 25% stake, Korea JoongAng Daily reported. Roughly 1 trillion won was used to buy shares and another 1 trillion to acquire new shares. There are different valuation numbers for this financing round. StartupIntros states 6.7 billion, whereas Bloomberg's figure is above 10 trillion won (9 billion) based on people familiar with the matter. Yanolja did not disclose the valuation figure. As of July 2023, Forbes estimated Lee’s net worth at $1.2 billion, as reported by CNBC.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Blinkit, Zepto among 105 food businesses hit by Maharashtra FDA action ahead of Diwali; food worth Rs 1.35 crore seized
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 105 food businesses, including Blink Commerce Pvt Ltd and Zepto
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 105 food businesses, including Blink Commerce Pvt Ltd and Zepto Ltd, and ordered seven establishments to shut operations after detecting multiple food safety violations during a special inspection drive ahead of Diwali.The two-day crackdown on November 4 and 5 also led to the seizure of nearly 39.5 tonnes of food articles worth Rs 1.35 crore across the state.According to an official statement, the suspended licences included 39 establishments in the Nashik division, 28 in Mumbai, 20 in Pune, 15 in Amravati, two in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and one in Thane.The seven establishments directed to stop operations included three in Pune, two in Amravati, and one each in Mumbai and the Konkan division.The list of establishments facing licence suspension included Blink Commerce Pvt Ltd and Zepto Ltd in Mumbai, along with food manufacturers, sweet shops, hotels, restaurants and caterers, the regulator said.The inspections revealed several violations, including unhygienic manufacturing and storage conditions, improper food handling and packaging, inadequate pest control, absence of temperature-control arrangements and failure to maintain mandatory records and certificates.During the two-day inspection drive, the FDA seized 39,485.42 kg of food articles worth Rs 1.35 crore from more than 70 establishments. The seized products included mawa, khoa, paneer, ghee, edible oils, farsan, dry fruits and various sweets.The Pune division recorded the highest seizure, with 14,429.7 kg of food articles worth Rs 49.36 lakh. The Konkan division reported seizures worth Rs 32.52 lakh, followed by Nashik at Rs 28.35 lakh, the food safety regulator said.Gutkha, pan masala worth Rs 7.96 lakh seizedThe administration also seized prohibited products, including gutkha and pan masala, worth Rs 7.96 lakh from three locations.Three FIRs were registered and two people arrested in connection with the seizures.Two vehicles worth Rs 4.70 lakh were also seized, while two establishments were sealed, the statement said.Among the establishments directed to stop business operations were Rajdhani Biryani Centre in Mumbai, Aaradhana Dryfruit Sweets in Bhiwandi in Thane district, and three food establishments in Pune.The FDA clarified that establishments whose licences have been suspended cannot carry out food business operations during the suspension period.(With PTI inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Recruits hail JSSC-CGL verdict as victory for hard work and perseverance
articles.summary: Jharkhand HC upholds JSSC-CGL recruitment exams, rejects blanket cancellation; directs govt to continue probe into irregularities as recruits hail verdict and Reform Manch protests.
articles.body: Ranchi: Ahead of Diwali, Jharkhand high court’s verdict upholding the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission-Combined Graduate Level (JSSC-CGL) recruitment examinations brought a sense of relief to recruits and their families, ending months of uncertainty over jobs they had secured after years of preparation.The court, however, made it clear that the relief would not come at the cost of accountability. It directed the state govt to continue its probe into alleged irregularities in the examinations and take action, after due process, against candidates found guilty of wrongdoing. At the same time, it rejected the demand for blanket cancellation of the recruitment exercise.Members of the JSSC-CGL batch welcomed the judgment, calling it a victory for “hard work, perseverance and truth”. In a statement issued after the verdict, they thanked the judiciary for the “historic judgment” and said they were committed to serving Jharkhand with honesty.“We thank the judiciary for the historic judgment. We are committed to serving the state with honesty,” the group said.The order, however, did little to calm the agitation against the recruitment process. JPSC-JSSC Reform Manch, one of the groups that spearheaded a month-long protest demanding cancellation of the examination and structural changes in recruitment, rejected the verdict.Speaking during a social media live session, outfit functionary Kunal Pratap said the outcome was expected “the way things were rushed”. He added that the group would continue its fight through “various means”, asserting that justice would ultimately be delivered.The verdict comes against the backdrop of an ongoing CID investigation into alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by Jharkhand Public Service Commission and JSSC. Since Aug, the agency has arrested more than two dozen people, including former JPSC chairperson L Khiangte.The probe is yet to reach its logical conclusion, leaving the controversy far from over.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Canada’s 2027–29 immigration plan: Temporary resident intake remains tightly controlled, while 2 lakh in-Canada residents get a pathway to PR
articles.summary: Canada has signalled that it is in no hurry to loosen its immigration controls.
articles.body: Canada has signalled that it is in no hurry to loosen its immigration controls. Its newly announced Immigration Levels Plan for 2027–2029 keeps the intake of new temporary residents at 3.70 lakh annually, comprising 2.20 lakh workers and 1.50 lakh international students for each of the three years. The immigration levels plan released last year for 2026-2028 had pegged the same figures. The overall annual target for permanent residents also remains unchanged at 3.80 lakh for each of the next three years.Significantly, the government has announced additional room to transition up to 2 lakh people (this applies to specific cohort groups) already in Canada to permanent residence (PR) in 2027, through a special time-limited measure.The cohort groups are: Up to one lakh workers and their accompanying families who meet selected provincial or federal programme requirements, and another one lakh people under humanitarian and family-reunification categories, including applicants from Hong Kong and Ukraine, and certain spouses, partners and dependent children of Canadians and permanent residents.The emphasis is increasingly on economic immigration, regional labour-market requirements and retaining people who are already contributing to the Canadian economy.The plan, announced in the wee hours of Friday morning (India time) as part of Budget 2026, reflects the government's continuing effort to bring the temporary-resident population below 5% of Canada's total population (of 4.18 crore) by the end of 2027, while keeping permanent-resident admissions below 1% of the population beyond 2027.The government says the number of non-permanent residents has declined over the past two years and population growth is now at its slowest annual rate in over a century. It maintains that stabilising immigration levels will give housing, healthcare and other public services time to catch up with population growth.Gurpreet Oshan, regulated Canadian immigration consultant (RCIC), said the plan signals a continued recalibration of Canada's immigration system, with a stronger emphasis on managing temporary-resident numbers while maintaining permanent immigration as an important part of its economic strategy."Canada is not closing its doors to immigration. Rather, it is moving towards a more controlled and targeted system, where eligibility for permanent residence will increasingly depend on how closely an applicant's profile aligns with the country's priorities," she said.Temporary foreign workers: The target for new temporary worker arrivals is set at 2.20 lakh annually for 2027, 2028 and 2029. This comprises 1.70 lakh under the International Mobility Program (IMP) and 50,000 under the Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP).The distinction is important. The International Mobility Program (IMP) covers work permits that are exempt from the Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) requirement. These include permits issued under international agreements, intra-company transfers, post-graduation work permits and certain open work permits for eligible family members, among other categories. The Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP), on the other hand, enables employers to hire foreign workers to fill temporary labour shortages when qualified Canadians or permanent residents are unavailable. Employers generally need a positive LMIA to demonstrate this.The government is looking to attract workers with skills that complement Canada's domestic workforce, particularly in sectors facing persistent labour shortages. It also proposes reforms to Express Entry and federal economic programmes to identify candidates whose experience and qualifications better match labour-market requirements.Rattandeep Singh, RCIC, pointed out that the worker intake target remains controlled even as the government makes room for people already in Canada to transition to permanent residence.“New worker arrivals are set at 2.2 lakh a year, and most of those are LMIA-exempt. But temporary residents are still 6.7% of Canada’s population, against a target of under 5% by the end of 2027. The government expects many permit holders to transition to permanent residence, and many to leave. Workers already in Canada need a permanent residence plan now, not when their permit is about to expire,” he said.Talha Mohani, RCIC, believes that the new approach marks a decisive shift towards retaining talent already in Canada. He cautioned that the 2 lakh transition spaces should not be interpreted as an automatic route to permanent residence for everyone holding a temporary work permit."Inland competition will reach an all-time peak," he said, pointing out that the number of temporary foreign workers already in Canada is substantial compared with the spaces being made available – statically only 20-25% will secure a spot before their work permit expires . Workers will need to align their profiles with regional labour-market requirements, including healthcare, skilled trades and high-wage occupations.Mohani also believes that provinces will have a greater say in determining which workers are retained. The new measure provides for up to one lakh workers already in Canada, along with their accompanying family members, to transition to permanent residence through Express Entry mechanism and provincial nominee programmes (PNPs) in collaboration with provinces and territories.International students: For international students, the annual target of new arrivals remains at 1.50 lakh for each of the three years. This indicates that Canada is continuing with a restrictive approach to international student admissions, rather than returning to the much higher intake levels seen in earlier years.The targets represent new arrivals under the International Student Program, covering students pursuing courses of six months or longer at designated learning institutions (DLIs).Oshan said that the reduced intake reflects a more restrictive environment for international students. "Studying in Canada does not guarantee a pathway to permanent residence," she cautioned.For Indian students, the implications are twofold. Admission opportunities will remain limited, while the ability to secure permanent status after completing studies will increasingly depend on qualifications, work experience and alignment with Canada's economic priorities.Permanent residents: Canada will maintain its permanent-resident admission target at 3.80 lakh annually through 2029. These admissions include those who are already working or studying in Canada, not just new arrivals. However, the composition of these admissions reflects the government's emphasis on economic immigration.The economic category accounts for a little over 2.4 lakh admissions annually, or 64% of the total. Family reunification is allocated 81,000 spaces, while refugees and protected persons account for 49,300. A further 5,000 spaces are earmarked for humanitarian and compassionate cases and other categories.One notable shift is the increased allocation to the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), which is set at 95,000 annually. The Federal High Skilled category, which includes the Federal Skilled Worker Program, Federal Skilled Trades Program and Canadian Experience Class, has an annual target of one lakh.This reinforces the growing importance of provincial selection in Canada's economic immigration strategy. The government has also announced increases in the targets for the Rural Community Immigration Program, from 5,500 in 2027 to 6,500 in 2029, and is making the Rural Community Immigration Pilot permanent.Mohani believes that provinces will exercise greater influence over economic immigration, particularly as Canada seeks to retain workers whose skills match regional requirements.Francophone immigration: Another important area is Francophone immigration outside Quebec. The government intends to raise the proportion of French-speaking permanent residents admitted outside Quebec from 9.5% in 2027 to 10.5% in 2028 and 12% in 2029. In absolute numbers, this represents approximately 31,825 admissions in 2027, rising to 40,200 by 2029.Rattandeep believes French-language proficiency will remain one of the strongest advantages for candidates seeking permanent residence. He advises temporary residents in Canada to consider learning French as part of their longer-term immigration strategy.New pathway for up to 2 lakh people already in Canada: Perhaps the most significant new announcement accompanying the levels plan is a time-limited measure to transition up to 2 lakh people already living in Canada to permanent residence during 2027.The measure is divided into two cohorts:Workers cohort: Up to 1 lakh people already in Canada, together with accompanying family members, will be transitioned to permanent residence in collaboration with provinces and territories. Additional PNP spaces will be allocated to provinces, which can nominate workers meeting their regional labour-market needs. Provinces can also identify eligible applicants already in the inventories of selected federal programmes, including the Atlantic Immigration Program, Start-up Visa Program, Self-Employed Persons Program, Agri-Food Pilot and home-care worker programmes.Humanitarian cohort: Up to 1 lakh people already in Canada will be transitioned to permanent residence. This includes applicants under the Hong Kong permanent residence pathways and the Ukraine Family Reunification Pathway, people already found eligible on humanitarian and compassionate grounds, and certain in-Canada applications from spouses, common-law partners and dependent children of Canadian citizens and permanent residents.The government says the initiative will help fulfil existing humanitarian commitments, keep families together and reduce application backlogs. It also expects to bring spousal sponsorship processing times closer to 12 months for applicants destined for provinces and territories outside Quebec.However, applicants should not assume that the new measure creates an open pathway for all temporary residents. IRCC has identified specific existing programmes and application inventories, and the detailed eligibility and selection processes will determine who benefits.What it means for Indian applicants: The 2027–2029 plan reinforces Canada's shift from high-volume immigration towards more selective admissions and the retention of talent already in the country.For Indian students aspiring to study in Canada, the annual intake cap of 1.50 lakh means that competition will remain significant. Those already studying or working in Canada will need to pay greater attention to the pathways available for transitioning to permanent residence.For temporary workers, provincial nomination, in-demand occupations, Canadian work experience and French-language proficiency could assume greater importance. Overseas applicants, meanwhile, will need to assess their profiles more carefully against Canada's economic and regional requirements.As Mohani summed up, Canadian immigration has moved from volume-driven recruitment to "precision-driven talent retention".The message is clear: Canada continues to need immigrants, but it is becoming increasingly particular about the skills it seeks, the numbers it admits and the people it wants to retain.EndsImmigration Levels for Permanent ResidentsYou use AI every day.
